clue.text: Nearest one can come for a close-up shot

definitions.text: Nearest one can come for a close-up shot

parts.words: Nearest one can come for a close-up shot
parts.note: a shot fired from so close the muzzle almost touches the target is the shortest distance a gunman can manage; 'close-up shot' pretends to be photography

explanation.surface: A photographer asks how near they can get for a close-up picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close-up shot' suggests a camera, but the shot is from a gun fired at the smallest possible distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun fired with the muzzle nearly touching its target is at the closest possible firing distance.

clue.text: A Roman who is not acceptable

definitions.text: A Roman who is not acceptable

parts.words: A Roman who is not acceptable
parts.note: the Latin phrase for an unwelcome individual, which is literally a 'person not pleasing', so it is Roman in language rather than in birth

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman citizen is turned away as unwelcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Roman' seems to be a citizen of Rome; it really means a Latin expression describing an unwelcome person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin diplomatic term labels someone, often an expelled diplomat, as unwelcome in a country.

clue.text: He doesn't believe I name the revolutionary leader

parts.note: Fidel Castro led the Cuban revolution

explanation.surface: A doubter says he names the revolutionary leader himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbeliever, someone without religious faith, is a man who doesn't believe.

clue.text: Thanks Kelvin for a piece of work

parts.note: TA is British informal for thank you, and the plural 'thanks' gives TAS
K is the symbol for the kelvin unit of temperature

explanation.surface: Someone thanks Kelvin for a job he has done.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thanks; the plural form matches 'Thanks', giving TAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A job or assignment to be done is a piece of work.

clue.text: Soothe infant (not first-born) with a song

parts.note: to lull is to soothe or calm

indicators.note: not first-born says the opening letter of the word for infant is dropped

parts.note: a baby is an infant

explanation.surface: A parent calms a younger child by singing to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not first-born' seems to describe a younger child, but it says BABY loses its first letter, leaving ABY.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle song sung to send a child to sleep is a kind of song.

clue.text: Additional officer, an employee of the press

parts.note: new can mean additional, as in a new recruit
SM is the abbreviation for sergeant major, a senior army rank
taken as written

explanation.surface: An extra officer is taken on, someone who works for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter or journalist is someone employed by the press.

clue.text: Some pressure Lydia exerted on trust

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Lydia is put under some pressure regarding a matter of trust.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on someone is to place your trust in them, so the phrase 'exerted on trust' describes leaning on them.

clue.text: The lion represented on a stone artefact

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lion is depicted carved on an ancient stone object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' looks like depiction, but it signals rearranging THE LION.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool or object made of stone in the Neolithic period is a stone artefact.

clue.text: Voters' liberation?

parts.note: granting people the right to vote, which also once meant freeing a slave, so it is a liberation that makes voters

explanation.surface: A slogan asks whether voters are being set free.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for giving the vote also has an older sense of setting free, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Granting the right to vote frees people into citizenship, and the word once meant release from slavery.

clue.text: Option to exchange the seal fur

indicators.note: exchanging swaps things around, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone offers the choice of trading a seal's fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to exchange' signals that SEAL FUR is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: First refusal is a right to choose before others, so a refusal can be an option.

clue.text: Rich spa isn't working

parts.note: a well is a mineral spring, as at a spa
a machine that is off is not working

explanation.surface: A wealthy resort's spa has broken down.
explanation.definitionFit: Being comfortably off financially means being wealthy.

clue.text: Probability of inequality

definitions.meaning: ... can mean a difference or disparity, as in being at ...

explanation.surface: A statistician weighs up the chance of unfairness.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting chances express probability, and things that are uneven or odd show disparity.

clue.text: Lucky, but likely to become stuck perhaps

definitions.meaning: covered in jam, so sticky and liable to get stuck

explanation.surface: Someone is fortunate but may end up trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: JAMMY is British slang for lucky; the second sense is literal, smeared with jam and so sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for fortunate, and literally sticky with fruit preserve.

clue.text: Traveller needs it as returning after six

indicators.note: after puts the turned word behind the numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: returning means the word as is read backwards

explanation.surface: A traveller needs a document when coming back after six.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport endorsement allowing entry to a country is something an international traveller requires.

clue.text: Welcome cry

definitions.meaning: to welcome someone is to receive them warmly

explanation.surface: A shout of welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots, to greet means to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: To receive visitors warmly, and the Scots verb for weeping.

clue.text: Hard getting a number one in Vietnam

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Things are tough when you are the top player in Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Vietnam is a place found in that country.

clue.text: Coming from gallery with abnormal sensitivity

indicators.note: abnormal means out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something from an art gallery brings on an unusual reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abnormal' looks like part of the definition, but it signals rearranging GALLERY.
explanation.definitionFit: An immune overreaction to pollen or food is a bodily sensitivity.

clue.text: Denial that a style related to a Biblical time

parts.note: no is a denial
chic means stylishness

explanation.surface: A refusal says a fashion belongs to an ancient scriptural era.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the patriarch who built the ark, so relating to an early scriptural period.

clue.text: Place a heavy burden on reporters after the operation

indicators.note: after puts the reporters behind the operation

parts.note: the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Journalists weigh heavily on someone after surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh down or tyrannise people is to burden them heavily.

clue.text: Penny and I rob another church of bagpipe music!

indicators.note: another means a different version, so the letters of rob are rearranged

explanation.surface: Penny and a friend raid a second church to steal its pipe tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' signals rearranging ROB to BRO; PIBROCH is classical music for the Scottish Highland bagpipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal theme-and-variations piece for the Highland pipes is a kind of bagpipe music.

clue.text: Dispute after dispute for the winger

indicators.note: after puts the first-named quarrel behind the second

parts.note: to spar is to argue
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: One argument follows another over a wing player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a football player, but here it is anything with wings, a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bird has wings, so it is a winger in crossword fashion.

clue.text: One quit bad coaching for a dish of dumplings

indicators.note: bad means poorly arranged, so the remaining letters are rearranged
quit says the letter for one leaves the word coaching

parts.note: A means one

explanation.surface: A man gave up poor coaching to make a pasta dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quit' takes A out of COACHING, leaving COCHING; 'bad' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Small Italian potato dumplings are served as a dish.

clue.text: Exploded. That's bad

definitions.meaning: a bomb that went off has exploded

explanation.surface: Something blew up, and that is a shame.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonated bomb has blown up, and spoiled milk has turned sour.

clue.text: Hat, cheap sort with gold finish

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A cheap kind of hat with a gilded finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' signals rearranging CHEAP to CHAPE; 'finish' puts AU last. CHAPEAU is French for hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a hat is used in English for a headpiece.

clue.text: Pass the fish

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the fish to be handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: To go past something, and a small coastal fish species.

clue.text: Haggard one in France trapped by a gun

indicators.note: trapped by means caught inside the word for gun

parts.note: gat is slang for a pistol
UN is French for one

explanation.surface: A haggard Frenchman is held at gunpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean and exhausted looking is what haggard and gaunt both mean.

clue.text: Tempo of piano expert

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert pianist's speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The speed at which a piece moves is its rate or tempo.

clue.text: Large number possessed land

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
had means possessed

explanation.surface: A huge number owned the territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The African country is a nation, a land.

clue.text: Employed by someone else first

explanation.surface: Someone is hired, but another person had them first.
explanation.definitionFit: Put to work, and second-hand, as of a car.

clue.text: One more, different one

explanation.surface: Ordering an extra one, but a different kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra one of the same, or an alternative of a different kind.

clue.text: Old boy's seen and heard to be blue

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: heard means the word seen is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like SCENE

explanation.surface: A former pupil has been spotted and overheard being rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' here means indecent, not sad or a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes or films are indecent and rude.

clue.text: One's certain to be without it when fully enlightened

definitions.text: One's certain to be without it when fully enlightened

parts.words: One's certain to be without it when fully enlightened
parts.note: complete certainty means having no doubt; full light leaves no shade, so enlightenment removes the dark patch

explanation.surface: A sage reflects that full enlightenment brings certainty.
explanation.walkthrough: Being certain beyond doubt, and full light casting no shade, are both read from 'fully enlightened'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sure beyond question is being without the slightest uncertainty.
